segment_summaries.content: Permutation-group polynomial examples: Lagrange genus domains, elementary symmetric functions, resultant R0 = ±1, involution form, and the Galois form of the group.
segment_summaries.choices: Kept historical Lagrange/Galois vocabulary visible while translating into modern integral-domain language.

segment_summaries.content: Regular systems S_{n1}, mapping to one algebraically independent polynomial, leading coefficient a0 as nonzero resultant, and existence of an integrality basis for all such systems.
segment_summaries.choices: Emphasized finite integrality basis, including the infinite one-variable polynomial-system case.

segment_summaries.content: Specialization to relatively integral domains G_{n1}; the Lüroth function is a polynomial and gives the integrality basis.
segment_summaries.choices: Maintained Lüroth theorem/function vocabulary and modernized linearly fractional dependence.

segment_summaries.content: Quadratic-form projective invariants as a final example; the determinant is the Lüroth function of the invariant field.
